title: The third-band prediction gain for Gaia20cdd depends on its deep 2022 dip
abstract: We test whether g-r colour improves independent i-band prediction for Gaia20cdd. We use 159 published ZTF three-band nights from 2018-2024 and leave out one year at a time. A colour plane has RMS 0.0533 mag, versus 0.0737 for one line and 0.1317 for a quadratic depth curve. After removing 2022, the line and plane both give 0.020 mag. A 30-day block interval for the paired mean squared error gain over the line includes zero. With all bands within two hours, the RMS difference falls to 0.0036 mag. A model trained before 2022 leaves a mean i-depth residual of +0.0825 mag on 13 deep nights in 2022. Colour helps describe the sample, but the prediction gain depends on one deep event. The test does not establish one fixed pair of grain laws across episodes. Sparse i sampling, exposure timing, detections-only data, and depth extrapolation limit the result. We provide code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and verified retrieval instructions.

display.caption: Prediction error by omitted year and sample. Most of the pooled colour gain comes from the deep 2022 event.
